issues.failure_explanation: The time-Lipschitz bound compares V(t,mu) and V(s,mu) as though the law stayed at mu over [s,t]. It ignores the displacement of the state law by the noise and the control, which the DPP requires one to control. The Ito-Kunita-Wentzell formula is then applied with d_t V when only a.e. differentiability in t, for each mu, is known. Differentiating the resulting identity at s=t requires continuity of d_t V, which is the very conclusion sought. The classical-solution claim is therefore not established.

issues.failure_explanation: For the uniform measure on the unit circle, the quadratic part of iint gives 1 and the log part 0, so G=1/2. For the uniform measure on the unit disk the parts are 1/2 and 1/4, so G=3/8<1/2. Hence the circle is not the minimizer. The value 0.75 is twice the disk energy and is inconsistent with the stated 1/2 prefactor; the N-convergence plot subtracts this value.
